minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  The Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Next Beverly Hills Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Thursday, January 18, 2024
  6:30 PM
MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  January 18, 2024 / 6:30 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Julian Gold, Vice Mayor Lester Friedman, Next Beverly Hills Chair
  Charles Smith, Next Beverly Hills Vice Chair Ellen Labbe, Deputy City
  Manager Kieth Sterling, Public Health Senior Policy & Management
  Administrator Gabriella Yap, Director of Community Services Stephanie
  Harris, Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce President & CEO Todd
  Johnson, Chamber of Commerce Director of Membership Michelle Green,
  Sustainability Chair Ariel Ouziel, Art Chair Melody Emrani, Cultural and
  heritage Commission Member Craig Corman

  1) Public Comment:

  Members of the public were given the opportunity to directly address the Committee on
  any item not listed on the agenda.

  None.

  2) Welcome & Introductions:
  a. Introductions by Chamber President Todd Johnson
  b. Presentation about the Chamber of Commerce by Chamber President Todd
  Johnson
  i. 35 board members representing most business entities in the city.
  ii. Nearly 800 members of which 35% are Business & Professional Services,
  20% Medical, Health, & Wellness, 12% Restaurants & Hotels, 9% Retail,
  5% Arts, Culture, & Entertainment, 5% Government, Utilities, &
  Infrastructure.
  iii. About 40% of businesses join the Chamber for networking purposes, about
  20% join for community involvement, about 13% for businesses credibility,
  about 10% for promotional opportunities, and 5% for advocacy.
  iv. The Chamber has numerous events & programs for members.
  c. The Chamber is an independent nonprofit organization that is contracted to the
  City. 1/3 of the budget comes from City contracts and the rest come from
  alternative sources.
  d. The Chamber works to facilitate relationships between the private sector and the
  city.
 Highlights for January 18, 2024
Recreation & Parks Commission

  3) NEXT Beverly Hills Mission Statement:
  a. NEXT Beverly is a committee of talented young business leaders, chartered by the
  Mayor and the City of Beverly Hills to engage residents between the ages of 25 &
  45 through innovative initiatives that address their lifestyles, economic, and civic
  needs to inspire them to make Beverly Hills a better place for all.
  b. The age range has expanded from the mission statement to include both younger
  and older opinions than that initial range.
  c. Introductions
  d. Gabriella Yap is leaving her position with the City of Beverly hills to become the
  Assistant City Manager of La Habra.

  4) New Business
  a. In response to a proposition to bring the opera to Beverly Hills, Stephanie
  mentioned the process for partnering with the city to enable that.
  b. Discussion about MADE Beverly Hills and a potential Partnership between MADE
  Palm Springs and NEXT for a discount code for attendance.
  c. Concerns raised by South Beverly Residents about the focus of BOLD and Holiday
  Lighting on the Triangle versus South Beverly.
  d. This has been brought to the attention of the city and they are taking steps that will
  coincide with the replacement of décor that has reached the end of its usable
  lifespan.
  e. Next Night 2024 is currently planned for October.
  f. Following a resident’s concern over pesticide usage, NEXT connected Public
  Works with a nonprofit that specializes in organics. They have had one meeting
  and are still in the discussion phase, but initial feedback suggests it would not
  come at a monetary cost, but solely one of time.
  g. The clothing drive was pushed from January 6th to February 11th. It is located at
  the main fire station and runs from 10:00 AM to noon.
  h. The tour of the Hydroponics Garden has been narrowed down to either February
  25th or March 3rd.
  i. The city has a sustainability manager who works to ensure that city events are
  sustainable.
  j. The Arts and Culture Commission put on a bi-annual art show and a monthly art
  walk. The city is also willing to look at hosting a painting in the park event.
  k.

  5) Current Business

  None

  6) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: January 18, 2024 / 7:35 PM
